lines.speaker: Charon
lines.text: Listen. Here is the situation. The boat, as you can see, is small, unsound, and mostly leaks. If it lists to one side, over it goes. And now here you all are at once, every one of you bringing luggage. If you get aboard with all that, I am afraid you may regret it later—especially those of you who cannot swim.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: So what do we do if we want a decent crossing?

lines.speaker: Charon
lines.text: I’ll tell you. They board naked. All this surplus goes on the shore. Even then the ferry will barely take them. And you, Hermes, from now on, see to it that nobody gets admitted unless he is stripped clean and has thrown away the furnishings, as I said. Stand by the gangplank, inspect them, and make them board naked.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Good. We’ll do that. — Who is this first one?

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Me. Menippus. And look, Hermes: my satchel and stick have gone straight into the lake. I did not even bring my cloak, which was thoughtful of me.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Get aboard, Menippus, best of men. Take the front seat beside the helmsman, up high, so you can inspect the lot of them. Now, who is this handsome fellow?

lines.speaker: Charon
lines.text: Charmoleos of Megara. Very popular. A kiss from him cost two talents.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Then take off the beauty, and the lips with all the kisses on them, and the thick hair, and the blush on your cheeks, and the whole skin. There. Much lighter. Board.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: And you there in the purple cloak and diadem, looking thunderous. Who are you supposed to be?

lines.speaker: Lampichus
lines.text: Lampichus, tyrant of Gela.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Then why have you turned up carrying all this, Lampichus?

lines.speaker: Lampichus
lines.text: Why? Should a tyrant come here naked, Hermes?

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: A tyrant, certainly not. A corpse, absolutely. Put it down.

lines.speaker: Lampichus
lines.text: There. The wealth is thrown away.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Throw away the conceit too, Lampichus, and the looking-down-on-people. If those come crashing in with you, they’ll sink the ferry.

lines.speaker: Lampichus
lines.text: At least let me keep the diadem and the robe.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: No. Those too.

lines.speaker: Lampichus
lines.text: Fine. What else? I’ve put everything down, as you see.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: The cruelty, the stupidity, the violence, the rage. Put those down as well.

lines.speaker: Lampichus
lines.text: There. I am stripped clean.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Board. And you—the fat one, all meat—who are you?

lines.speaker: Damasias
lines.text: Damasias the athlete.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Yes, you look it. I’ve seen you often enough in the wrestling schools.

lines.speaker: Damasias
lines.text: Yes, Hermes. But take me aboard; I’m naked.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Not naked, my good man, not with all that flesh wrapped round you. Take it off. You will swamp the boat if you put just one foot over the side. And throw away those victory wreaths, and the herald’s announcements.

lines.speaker: Damasias
lines.text: There. Now I am truly naked, as you see, and the same weight as the other corpses.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Much better, being weightless. Board. And you, Craton: put down the money. The softness too, and the luxury. Don’t bring the grave-clothes, don’t bring your ancestors’ titles. Leave your family, your reputation, any public proclamations in your honour, and the inscriptions on your statues. Don’t mention the large tomb they built over you either. Even remembering these things adds weight.

lines.speaker: Craton
lines.text: Not willingly. But I’ll throw it away. What else can I do?

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Well now. You there, in armour. What do you want? And why are you carrying that trophy?

lines.speaker: General
lines.text: Because I won, Hermes. I distinguished myself. The city honoured me.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Leave the trophy above ground. In Hades we have peace; nobody will need weapons.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: And who is this solemn specimen—just look at the posture—preening, eyebrows hoisted, absorbed in Deep Thought, with the long beard hanging down?

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Some philosopher, Hermes. Or rather a fraud packed full of prodigies. Strip him too. You’ll find plenty of ridiculous things hidden under that cloak.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: You: put down the pose first. Then all of this. Good Zeus, what a load of imposture he’s carrying. And ignorance, quarrelsomeness, vanity, impossible questions, thorny arguments, tangled notions—plus a great deal of wasted labour, no small quantity of drivel, nonsense, pettiness—by Zeus, and this bit of gold here, and sensuality, shamelessness, anger, luxury, softness. Don’t think I missed them, however carefully you hid them. Put down lying too, and conceit, and the belief that you are better than everyone else. If you boarded carrying all that, what fifty-oared warship could take you?

lines.speaker: Philosopher
lines.text: Then I put them down, since you insist.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Make him put down that beard as well, Hermes. Heavy and hairy, as you see. Five minas of hair at least.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Good point. Put that down too.

lines.speaker: Philosopher
lines.text: And who is going to cut it off?

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Menippus here will take one of the shipwright’s axes and chop it off, using the gangplank as a block.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: No, Hermes. Hand me a saw. That would be funnier.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: The axe will do. There. Excellent. Now you look almost human, once the goat-stink has been removed.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Shall I take a little off the eyebrows too?

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Please. He’s been lifting them above his forehead; I don’t know what he thought he was elevating. What’s this? Crying, you filth? Losing your nerve at death? Get aboard anyway.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: He has one more thing under his arm. The heaviest thing of all.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: What, Menippus?

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Flattery, Hermes. It was very useful to him in life.

lines.speaker: Philosopher
lines.text: Then you, Menippus, put down your freedom, your frank speech, your freedom from grief, your courage, and your laughter. You’re the only one laughing.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Absolutely not. Keep those. They’re light, very easy to carry, and useful for the descent.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: And you, the rhetorician: put down the endless flood of words, the antitheses, balanced clauses, periods, barbarisms, and the rest of the verbal ballast.

lines.speaker: Rhetorician
lines.text: Here. I put them down.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Good. Cast off the shore-lines, pull up the gangplank, haul in the anchor, spread the sail. Ferryman, keep the rudder straight. Let’s have a good passage.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Why are you whining, you fools—especially you, philosopher, with your beard freshly put to the torch?

lines.speaker: Philosopher
lines.text: Because, Hermes, I thought the soul was immortal.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: He’s lying. Something else is bothering him.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: What?

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: That he will no longer dine at expensive dinners; that he will no longer slip out at night with his head wrapped in his cloak, supposedly unseen, and make the rounds of the brothels; and that he will no longer deceive young men in the morning with his wisdom and take their money. That is what bothers him.

lines.speaker: Philosopher
lines.text: And you, Menippus? Aren’t you upset to be dead?

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: How could I be? I hurried to death without even being invited.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: But while we’re talking—don’t I hear shouting? Sounds like people yelling from earth.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Yes, Menippus, and not from just one place. Some have gathered in the assembly and are all laughing with pleasure at Lampichus’ death. His wife is being throttled by the women, and his little children, babies though they are, are being pelted by the boys with a generous supply of stones. Others in Sicyon are praising Diophantus the rhetorician, who is delivering funeral speeches over this man Craton. And by Zeus, Damasias’ mother is leading the women’s lament for Damasias, wailing beautifully. But you, Menippus, nobody is crying for you. You lie there by yourself in peace.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Not at all. In a moment you’ll hear the dogs howling most piteously over me, and the crows beating their wings when they gather to bury me.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: You’re a brave one, Menippus. Well, now that we’ve made land, the rest of you go straight on there to the court. The ferryman and I are going back for another load.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Good sailing, Hermes. Come on, the rest of us should move along. Why are you still hanging back? You’ll have to be judged either way. And they say the sentences are severe: wheels, stones, vultures. Everyone’s life will be put on display in exact detail.
